articles.title: Rayo y la Comunidad de Madrid chocan por la auditoría que decidirá la vuelta a Vallecas
articles.standfirst: Fuentes del club aseguran que la CAM tiene desde esta mañana un informe firmado por sus propios auditores que autoriza el regreso inmediato al estadio, mientras que la Comunidad lo desmiente tajantemente y sostiene que la auditoría no está completada
articles.summary: Fuentes del club aseguran que la CAM tiene desde esta mañana un informe firmado por sus propios auditores que autoriza el regreso inmediato al estadio, mientras que la Comunidad lo desmiente tajantemente y sostiene que la auditoría no está completada
articles.body: El regreso del Rayo Vallecano a Vallecas vuelve a quedar atrapado en un choque frontal de versiones entre el club franjirrojo y la Comunidad de Madrid. Según fuentes del Rayo, la CAM tiene desde esta mañana la auditoría firmada por sus propios auditores autorizando que el fútbol vuelva al estadio desde ya. La Comunidad, sin embargo, lo desmiente tajantemente y sostiene que esa auditoría todavía no está completada. El desencuentro abre un nuevo capítulo en una situación que sigue sin desbloquearse. En Vallecas entienden que, si existe una auditoría favorable y firmada por los auditores de la propia Comunidad, el regreso debería poder producirse de forma inmediata. Desde la CAM, en cambio, niegan que haya luz verde y mantienen que el proceso no ha terminado. En el Rayo se encuentran ahora en fase de estudio para conocer cuáles son los pasos legales a dar. El club considera que el escenario ha entrado en un punto delicado después de una mañana en la que, según sus fuentes, la auditoría ya estaría en poder de la Comunidad y avalaría la reapertura del estadio para la disputa de partidos. La preocupación en Vallecas va más allá del encuentro más inmediato. El temor dentro de la entidad franjirroja es que esta situación pueda alargarse y obligue al equipo a disputar más partidos lejos de su estadio. Una posibilidad que empieza a ganar peso mientras no haya una resolución definitiva. La Comunidad de Madrid mantiene una postura completamente distinta. Fuentes de la CAM desmienten tajantemente que la auditoría esté completada y niegan que exista ya una autorización definitiva para que el fútbol regrese a Vallecas. Ese choque mantiene bloqueado el regreso. El Rayo sostiene que la auditoría ya estaría firmada y sería favorable. La Comunidad insiste en que el informe sigue sin completarse y que, por tanto, no hay autorización para volver al estadio. En lo único en lo que coinciden las dos partes es en el escenario del próximo partido. Tanto el Rayo como la Comunidad confirman que el encuentro del martes ante el Espanyol se disputará en Butarque. El fútbol no volverá a Vallecas para ese partido. La incógnita, ahora, es si el desencuentro por la auditoría se resolverá a tiempo para evitar que el exilio franjirrojo se prolongue más allá de la próxima jornada.

articles.title: Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur blasts 'erratic, poor' performance as side fall to defeat ahead of play-offs
articles.summary: Leeds Rhinos lost the last two rounds of the regular season ahead of the Super League play-offs; They await to find out their semi-final opponents; The Super League play-offs begin on Friday September 18, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
In what was effectively the battle for the League Leaders' Shield, Wigan Warriors wiped the floor with Leeds in a 40-8 drubbing.

Wigan then completed the formality and wrapped up the domestic double with a 50-12 win over Catalans, keeping a treble firmly in their sights.

Meanwhile, Leeds finished with an 18-12 loss to Hull FC who will finish the season in 11th. It is not the time to run out of steam - Leeds now have a week's rest to figure out how to reset, recharge, and head into the semi-finals reinvigorated.

They will know who they face once Wakefield Trinity play Leigh Leopards on Friday September 18 and Warrington Wolves face Hull KR on Saturday September 19 in the Eliminators, live on Sky Sports .

They need to welcome their semi-final opponent to Headingley and make them feel like they are entering a fortress.

Leeds head coach Brad Arthur admitted that very element was missing in Round 27 and said it was simply "not good enough".

"We were a bit erratic at times. Some of our skill with the ball was very poor," Arthur said.

"We created more than enough opportunities. More than enough field position. Our forwards did more than enough on our edges and we were poor on our edges without execution."

It is clear that Arthur knows what the issues are but is there an easy fix?

He believes that will be down to individuals stepping things up and making sure, for one final time in 2026, that Headingley is too tough for whoever has to visit to ensure Leeds make it to Old Trafford for the first time since 2022.

"It's an individual thing. Our skill was poor. We created enough chances and had enough field position," he added.

"We have two weeks, new competition. But we're not happy with our performances at home. Not good enough. This place needs to be a tough place to come and play."

Wilkin: Leeds were shown their vulnerabilities and have not recovered

One thing that is key in sport is confidence. Leeds have had that in abundance until they have not.

It is a frailty laid bare by meeting a team who have been there, done that, and got the t-shirt in Wigan.

Leeds have not walked the walk in a very long time, their last Grand Final win coming back in 2017, and it is now "concerning" that they have not bounced back and that their coach believes it is a "skill and execution" issue.

"Leeds have strutted through the season with the confidence of looking like champions and feeling like champions," said Sky Sports Rugby League's Jon Wilkin.

"Last week I saw vulnerability and a weakness exposed by Wigan, who went straight over the top of them and said: 'You might well believe you're the business, but you're not'.

"It's just not happened for them. It's concerning.

"Wigan have got a deep confidence and history of being near the top. I don't think Leeds have got that yet. A champion team would react to such a humbling defeat to Wigan. Not only that, but I just don't think you get beaten so comprehensively."

"What will be a worry is Brad Arthur has highlighted skill and execution, saying that's the problem," added Sam Tomkins.

"That's the reason why they've been top for so long, they were good at the start, but they've not had it in the last month.

"If their execution is off and their skill and edge is off, that's what they hang their hat on. I think It's a worry. It's not an easy fix and there will be questions asked and it will be a tough couple of weeks."

articles.title: Super League play-offs: Dates, format, schedule as Wigan, Leeds, Wakefield, Leigh, Warrington, Hull KR vie for spot in Grand Final at Old Trafford
articles.summary: Wakefield will take on Leigh and Warrington face Hull KR in the play-offs; The winners will then face either Wigan Warriors or Leeds Rhinos in the semi-finals; The Super League play-offs begin on Friday September 18, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Wigan Warriors emphatically wrapped up a domestic double with a 50-12 win over Catalans Dragons to secure the League Leaders' Shield.

That adds to their Challenge Cup win and now, they are on the hunt for the treble if they can win in the big dance at the Grand Final.

They now get a week's rest, as do Leeds Rhinos who finished second despite their final-round loss to Hull FC.

The final league table top six finished as: Wigan Warriors, Leeds Rhinos, Warrington Wolves, Wakefield Trinity, Leigh Leopards, and Hull KR.

Now, there are four matches left until we know the final two. Until we know the two teams who will do battle to win the trophy everyone has been hunting.

The format now is simple. Third-place finisher Warrington will play Hull KR who finished sixth. Fourth-placed Wakefield will take on fifth-place finisher Leigh for a place in the semi-finals.

The lowest-ranked winner of those contests, so the team that finished lowest in the league table, will then take on Wigan Warriors.

The other team will face Leeds Rhinos in the second semi-final.

The Eliminators will take place across Friday September 18 and Saturday September 19.

Wakefield vs Leigh will take place on the Friday, with kick-off at 8pm live on Sky Sports .

Warrington vs Hull KR then takes place on the Saturday at 5.30pm, also live on Sky Sports .

Wigan Warriors and Leeds Rhinos know they are in the semi-finals and know exactly which days they will be playing on across Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26.

Leeds await their opponent for the Friday contest, with kick-off at 8pm.

Wigan Warriors also wait patiently to know who they will face on the Saturday, with kick-off at 5.30pm.

Both matches will be shown live on Sky Sports .

The winners of those two contests then advance to the Super League Grand Final at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3.

Six will be whittled down to two ready for the big dance.

articles.title: College Fantasy Football: Bold predictions for the weekend's Week 2 slate
articles.summary: It's time to get bold for Week 2 of the college fantasy football season!
articles.body:
Yahoo Sports College Football analysts Eric Froton and Nick Bromberg deliver their boldest college fantasy football predictions for the remaining Week 2 slate.

Being an also-ran program in the SEC can be a frustrating existence. Just ask South Carolina, which is coming off a dismal 4-8 campaign where the Gamecocks averaged just 22.7 points and 336 yards per game last season. So when SC plays an inferior opponent in a paycheck game, like this week against FCS Towson, it goes full Cobra Kai and shows no mercy whatsoever. In Week 1 the Gamecocks destroyed Kent State 57-0, and in Week 13 last year, hung an absurd 579 yards and 56 points on Coastal Carolina .

I think we see LaNorris Sellers score 4+ touchdowns and score 30+ fantasy points, which would firmly plant Sellers in CFF QB1 territory, making him a must-start. I also believe he hits rising star WR Nyck Harbor for two long touchdowns, with Harbor easily clearing the 20 fantasy-point mark.

Some teams take their foot off the gas against lower division programs and play backups early, however, with HC Shane Beamer's seat getting warm, I expect major fantasy production to come from South Carolina's starting offense before it takes on SEC foe Mississippi State next weekend. — Eric Froton

Clemson's opening game 51-10 evisceration at the hands of LSU and new head coach Lane Kiffin was approaching cataclysmic, leading to questions about whether Dabo Swinney can succeed in the new era of college football. This week, the Tigers are in a classic "get right" spot against a very capable Georgia Southern offense that averaged 28 PPG and ranked top-50 nationally in EPA/Play and success rate. Unfortunately, GaSo was saddled with one of the worst defenses in the country, ranking 135th in EPA/Rush and 122nd in 20+ yard plays allowed.

Clemson will be forced to press the pedal-to-the-metal and get back into a winning mindset before welcoming Bill Belichick's UNC defense to Memorial Stadium in Week 3. Starting RB Gideon Davidson is going to punch in two touchdowns and clear 100 rushing yards, while superstar WR Bryant Wesco Jr. clears 100 yards receiving with another score. GaSo's offense is pesky enough to keep Clemson's starters in through the third quarter, which means a long touchdown reception for WR TJ Moore, too.

In summation, I think all three of Clemson's top playmakers find the end zone after getting smothered by DC Blake Baker 's LSU defense, as the Tigers try to reclaim their offensive identity heading into ACC play. — Froton

Is a waiver-wire QB your key to Week 2 success?

Don't be afraid to grab a free-agent QB and immediately put him in your starting lineup in Week 2. Especially if his team is playing an overmatched opponent.

Louisville QB Lincoln Kienholz is rostered in just 6% of leagues. He scored over 35 points against Ole Miss and the Cardinals play FCS Villanova on Friday night. Florida 's Aaron Philo threw three TDs and ran for another in Week 1. The Gators have FCS Campbell in Week 2 and he's on just 4% of teams.

Even a player like Cincinnati's JC French, who scored over 30 points in the Bearcats' Week 1 win over Boston College is on just 1% of teams. And Cincy has Western Carolina in Week 2.

Starting a player like that may seem like a risk, but given their opponent, it might actually be a safe bet in Week 2. — Nick Bromberg

I don't think that Alabama's 227 rushing yards against East Carolina was a fluke. The Crimson Tide rushed for five touchdowns as QB Keelon Russell was the team's leading rusher in his first start with 86 yards and a TD.

RB Daniel Hill had just 47 yards on nine attempts but he scored two touchdowns against the Pirates. Hill is rostered in just 11% of leagues after Week 1 and will assuredly be added to more teams if Alabama's rushing success continues. And I think it will. Hill and freshman EJ Crowell — who is on 12% of teams — are going to become valuable fantasy players throughout the course of the season. Don't be afraid to be early rather than late. — Bromberg

articles.title: Ravens rule out LB Teddye Buchanan
articles.summary: The Ravens officially ruled out two players for Sunday's season opener against the Colts.
articles.body:
The Ravens officially ruled out two players for Sunday's season opener against the Colts.

Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and linebacker Teddye Buchanan will not play. Both are coming off season-ending injuries from 2025.

Madubuike's delayed return was previously reported when coach Jesse Minter gave the team's injury update during his news conference.

Buchanan was limited in practice all week. He tore the ACL and the meniscus in his right knee on Dec. 14 and sprained his LCL in the same knee.

He only returned to the practice field Aug. 17.

Trenton Simpson , listed as a co-starter on the depth chart, will start for Buchanan.

The Ravens, though, have only three healthy linebackers on their 53-player roster, so they are likely to elevate Carl Jones Jr. from the practice squad.

Wide receiver Devontez Walker (groin) is questionable after limited practices this week. Wide receiver Zay Flowers (hamstring) returned to full participation on Thursday and has no injury designation.

The team added defensive lineman Calais Campbell to the injury report as he took a rest day Friday.

articles.title: Why Rays might trade away their 3.10 ERA All-Star ace this offseason
articles.summary: This ace from the Rays might be on the move this winter.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays are sitting atop the American League with only a few weeks to go in the 2026 regular season. This club might be in for a deep playoff run as well.

But after the season comes to a close, the Rays are going to be tasked with some tough decisions to make. One of the biggest issues they'll need to resolve involves two pitchers in the starting rotation, both of whom are heading into the last year of their deals.

MLB.com's Mark Feinsand highlighted one of those pitchers, All-Star ace Shane McClanahan , as a potential trade option thanks to his injury history, his cheaper 2027 contract, and his looming free agency after the 2027 season.

Why Shane McClanahan could be traded by Rays this offseason

"McClanahan has pitched well this season after missing two years following Tommy John surgery, but he's entering his final year of arbitration prior to becoming a free agent, a time when Tampa Bay has typically looked to move players," Feinsand writes.

With McClanahan set to hit the open market soon, the Rays could look to trade their ace, getting back some valuable long-term assets as opposed to keeping McClanahan for the remainder of his deal and risk losing him in free agency for nothing.

The injury history of McClanahan might make a trade a little bit more challenging to pull off, but the injuries have likely lowered his 2027 salary to a more reasonable amount.

McClanahan was once a top pitcher in baseball before these recent injuries derailed his career. He has a 3.10 ERA for his big league career, including a 3.36 ERA during the 2026 season across 24 starts.

There is some risk for a team acquiring McClanahan, especially if the Rays demand a massive package in return for him this offseason if they trade him.

But the upside of the former Cy Young candidate might be too good for some of the top contenders eyeing pitching upgrades around baseball, like the Chicago Cubs and Atlanta Braves , to pass up.

The one thing that could hold the Rays back from trading McClanahan is if they decide instead to trade Drew Rasmussen , whose $20 million contract could lead the Rays to move on from him next season.

McClanahan is a name Rays fans should keep an eye on this upcoming offseason, as the trade rumors surrounding the left-handed ace could very well come to fruition.

articles.title: Super League: Wakefield Trinity beat Leigh Leopards to earn play-offs rematch as Warrington Wolves set up Hull KR clash
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves finished in third with their win and now will face Hull KR in the Eliminators; Wakefield Trinity and Leigh Leopards will clash again in the other Eliminator contest; The Super League play-offs begin on Friday September 18, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The two sides will clash again next week in the fourth vs fifth Eliminator contest but this time the contest will take place in Yorkshire on Friday September 18, live on Sky Sports .

The fourth-place finish is Wakefield's highest ever in the Super League season and is the latest sign of their resurgence under Daryl Powell after returning to the Super League in 2025.

Meanwhile, a 26-14 win for a young Warrington Wolves side over Toulouse Olympique saw them wrap up third spot and they will face Hull KR, who finished in sixth after a 36-12 loss to St Helens. That match will take place on Saturday September 19, also live on Sky Sports .

The winners of those two contests will then advance to the semi-finals for the chance to face either League Leaders' Shield winners Wigan Warriors or second-place Leeds Rhinos for a spot in the Grand Final at Old Trafford on October 3.

Wakefield make statement as Leigh cannot finish fight back

In the warm-up for the Eliminator match-up between Wakefield and Leigh Leopards, Tom Johnstone went over early for the visitors as they made the most of their own kick, Jake Trueman sending his winger sliding in for a 4-0 lead.

Two Max Jowitt penalties then came alongside a second try for the Wakefield winger that was the most spectacular of finishes, moving them 12-0 up.

Trueman then sent a message just before the break as he sent over a drop goal for a 13-0 advantage, the home Leigh faithful sombre knowing this was the exact contest they will play next week away from home.

Leigh Leopards came out chancing their arm in the second half and Owen Trout got them on the scoreboard.

It then looked like they were heading towards a comeback after Mason Lino was sent to the sin bin for a professional foul and they capitalised through Innes Senior with a brilliant finish on the edge to bring the score to 13-8.

However, Wakefield stood strong and with just three minutes left on the clock, Cam Scott powered over in the corner and Jowitt converted to wrap up a 19-8 win.

Leigh beat Wakefield in the play-offs in 2025 but if they are to do it again, it would mark their first win over Trinity this season.

Powell: It is time for us to show we are good enough

Wakefield Trinity head coach Daryl Powell speaking to Sky Sports...

"I thought the boys did us proud today. We had a sin-binning but then we were tough and courageous after that.

"We will dust ourselves down, learn from this, and get ready.

"I think both teams will have been talking about it being around play-off time and being ready for it.

"We probably left a couple of points on the field thanks to some desperate defence from Leigh.

"It is all about next week now. Leigh beat us last year in the play-offs, we were stinging from that, and we carried that into this year."

"I just think we have had some great lessons," he added.

"We have carried them through with us and we are a better team for having them at the end of the season.

"It is awesome- into the six and a great opportunity for us.

"Are we good enough? It is for us to show we are. It is for us to show we are capable of great things."

Warrington head coach Sam Burgess took a risk to rest the majority of his side, having made 11 changes, and opted for his young guns to see his side home in third position, and they did just that with a gusty victory.

Toulouse have impressed across 2026 under Sylvain Houles on their return to Super League and early on they had Warrington locked into a contest.

They went over first through Paul Ulberg, but an error on their own line allowed Aaron Lindop to capitalise.

The visitors hit back again through Mathieu Pons but on the stroke of half-time, Lachlan Webster levelled at 8-8. None of the four tries scored were converted.

Similarly to the first half, Toulouse were the first to go over again in the second period thanks to Romeo Tropis, but then Warrington took things up a notch.

After Max Wood barged over from short range, Lindop capitalised on another error for his second.

Even with a man down after Charlie McKler was sent to the sin bin for a high shot, the Wolves showed their grit and Josh Smith did incredibly to slide in on the end of a Leon Hayes kick.

Hayes converted three of the five efforts and Warrington now have Hull KR in their sights as they welcome them to the Halliwell Jones Stadium in a clash for a spot in the semi-finals.

Saints bid farewell to two modern legends as KR finish sixth

It was an emotional night in St Helens as they said goodbye to two modern-day legends, Mark Percival and Jonny Lomax, and they marked it with a 36-12 victory over Hull KR, who finish the season in sixth place.

They handed the former the captaincy for the first time in his career, a guard of honour forming as the pair made their way out onto the field.

However, their farewells also marked their earliest goodbye to a season in their history; after finishing seventh and taking on an inexperienced Hull KR side, they were expected to finish with a sizeable victory.

The Robins had welcomed back Mikey Lewis from his two-match ban but head coach Willie Peters had opted to rest his players ahead of the defence of their title.

The first half was written in the stars for the home side as Percival opened the scoring, then provided the assist for Lomax to mark Saints' second.

Just when you thought the storyline was done, Lomax barged over for his second on the stroke of half-time for an 18-0 lead.

Hull KR did hit back through Bill Leyland and a sensational solo effort from 18-year-old Flynn Holden on debut, but efforts from Deon Cross, Jacob Host, and Harry Robertson were enough to seal the comprehensive win as an era came to a fitting end at Saints.

articles.title: English Open: Shaun Murphy beats Judd Trump in final-frame decider
articles.summary: Shaun Murphy snatches a thrilling final-frame victory over Judd Trump to reach the semi-finals of the English Open.
articles.body:
Shaun Murphy snatched a thrilling final-frame victory over Judd Trump to reach the semi-finals of the English Open.

World number seven Murphy moved 5-4 ahead before Trump, the world number three, cleared 112 to take the match to a decider.

Murphy managed to overcome his English compatriot in a nervy final frame, helped by some deft safety play, to set up a semi-final against Mark Williams.

Williams withstood a fightback from fellow Welshman Liam Davies to book his spot in the semi-finals with a 6-3 victory.

Williams was level at 2-2 at the interval but pulled clear and eventually sealed his victory with a 112 clearance.

England's Kyren Wilson was left scoreless in the first three frames as Ding Junhui cruised to a 6-2 victory.

Wilson briefly threatened a comeback, winning the next two frames to reduce the deficit to 3-2, but China's Ding quickly regained control and took the final three frames to seal his place in the final four.

Ding will face Ali Carter in the semi-finals, who produced an excellent late display to edge past Zhou Yuelong 6-5 by winning three frames in a row.

Zhou had been leading 5-3, but Carter was able to turn it around from frame nine onwards, making the most of Zhou missing a routine yellow, then winning the next 80-39 before dominating in the decider.

Both semi-finals take place on Saturday, with Ding taking on Carter at 12:00 BST before Murphy faces Williams at 18:00.

articles.title: Kernel girls tennis wins fifth in a row
articles.summary: Sep. 11—MITCHELL — Mitchell High School girls tennis powered its way to an 8-1 victory on Thursday over Sioux Falls Washington in a dual at Hitchcock Park. I...
articles.body:
Sep. 11—MITCHELL — Mitchell High School girls tennis powered its way to an 8-1 victory on Thursday over Sioux Falls Washington in a dual at Hitchcock Park.

It was Mitchell's fifth dual win in a row, improving to 12-3 in dual contests this season.

In singles play, Mitchell won five of the six matches, led by Mia Larson's 6-0, 6-0 sweep at Flight 2. Elliot Smith was a 6-2, 6-2 winner at Flight 4 and Charlee Cimpl won 6-3, 6-3 at Flight 5 singles. Katie Morgan outlasted Madelyn Dahlmeier at No. 1 singles 6-4, 7-5 for key win and Sydney Love won 6-3, 5-7 and 10-2 at Flight 6 for a tough win.

Mitchell also swept all three doubles matches. Morgan and Ava Prunty were 6-0, 6-2 winners at Flight 1, while Larson and Smith won at Flight 2 by a score of 6-2, 6-3. Cimpl and Taryn Bultje were 3-6, 6-1 and 11-9 winners at Flight 3 doubles.

Mitchell will compete next on Tuesday, Aug. 15 in a triangular at Yankton against the host Gazelles and Sioux Falls Lincoln.

articles.title: Hammer and Rails Readers React Results: Purdue Football Expectations After Week 1
articles.summary: Did expectations for Purdue’s season change?
articles.body:
Less than 24 hours away from Purdue's week two game against Wake Forest it's time for a final look back at Purdue's week 1 game against Indiana State. This week I asked you all to tell me if Purdue's performance against the Sycamores changed your expectations for the rest of the season. It seemed like a good thing to ask given that I had already asked all of you how you graded Purdue's week 1 performance. The results were not great if you're Purdue.

As you can see the majority of respondents graded Purdue at a C. That's not what you want out of week 1 when you're playing a cupcake. So given that C grade I was curious if that changed expectations up or down. Of course. there was also the option for no change. So, let's take a look at the results.

A whopping 76% of respondents didn't change their expectations after week 1 which honestly seems very reasonable, rationale, and not at all okay for this current internet age. Those 76% are the well adjusted respondents. 22% revised their expectations down and those are the people who likely graded Purdue much lower than a C. Honestly, I don't blame them. articles.summary: The New York Yankees will get Clarke Schmidt back from Tommy John surgery soon. Yankees manager Aaron Boone told MLB.com’s Bryan Hoch that Schmidt will do on...
articles.body:
The New York Yankees will get Clarke Schmidt back from Tommy John surgery soon. Yankees manager Aaron Boone told MLB.com's Bryan Hoch that Schmidt will do one more rehab outing before being activated from the 60-day injured list.

That next outing will likely be with Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre. The Yankees have been very meticulous with Schmidt's rehab appearances, with multiple days off between each one. His next one will come on two days' rest.

Schmidt had been a reliable arm at the bottom of the Yankees' rotation. However, injuries have affected the last two seasons. The 30-year-old suffered a torn UCL in July 2025 and underwent Tommy John surgery. His return will mark 14 months since the injury.

Yankees Announce Latest Clarke Schmidt Injury Update

Given the current timeline, Clarke Schmidt won't be activated during the Mets series. Instead, he'll be back during their road trip against the Minnesota Twins and Arizona Diamondbacks . Most likely, he'll be activated on September 14, ahead of the Twins series opener.

Schmidt will likely return as a multiple-inning reliever. The Yankees can get a look at that for the final two weeks before deciding if they should roster him for the postseason. The decision could very much depend on their status for the Wild Card round.

Since Schmidt was on the 60-day injured list on September 1, the Yankees will have to petition the commissioner's office for postseason eligibility. He would have to replace an injured player who has spent the requisite number of days on the injured list. One such example is Giancarlo Stanton .

His long-term future with the Yankees may be in relief, for both this year and next. Since his injury, right-handers Cam Schlittler and Will Warren have emerged as reliable arms in the rotation. But that's a decision for Brian Cashman to make in November.

The New York Yankees enter their series against the New York Mets with an 84-62 record. Their chances of qualifying for the postseason are just about 100%, according to FanGraphs' Playoff Odds .

With the club sitting just three games back of the Tampa Bay Rays , the division is still in play. Especially when there are still four head-to-head games remaining.

The Yankees will likely need to sweep that series to win the division, however. Their odds of winning the division are less than 20%. But the Yankees have a chance now that Aaron Judge is back from injury.

Whoever wins the American League East will get home-field advantage through the World Series.

articles.title: Texas vs. Ohio State Picks, Odds, Predictions: Our Best Bets for College Football Week 2
articles.summary: Check out Texas Longhorns vs. Ohio State Buckeyes picks, odds, predictions and best bets for college football Week 2 on Sept. 12.
articles.body:
One of the biggest games of the 2026 college football season kicks off on Saturday when the No. 4 Texas Longhorns host the No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes.

With a spread of just 1.5 points, this matchup is shaping up to be one of the most entertaining games of the year to this point — and that's without the massive postseason implications that could be in play.

The Longhorns are once again National Championship contenders behind quarterback Arch Manning , who picked up some transfer portal weapons to play with over the offseason.

Manning's connection with Auburn transfer Cam Coleman is already apparent after the two connected for a touchdown in their season opener against Texas State.

On the other side, the Buckeyes are the favorites to win the national title (+500) thanks in large part to quarterback Julian Sayin and wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, who has racked up over 2,700 yards and 29 touchdowns in his career, including two scores already this season.

With Texas entering as a -1.5 underdog and the over/under set at a modest 49.5 points, who holds the advantage here?

Let's dive into our Texas vs. Ohio State picks and college football predictions for this Week 2 clash on Saturday, September 12.

Download the Action Network app for more expert picks and analysis!

Given the close spread and ranking between the No. 1 and No. 4 teams in the country, it's no surprise that our staff is split on this line. Six of our 11 experts side with Ohio State +1.5, while the remaining five back Texas -1.5 at home.

As it stands after Week 1, respected public power ratings are just as split between these two teams, most of which have them first and second. FPI, TeamRankings and Sagarin favor Texas, while SP+, FEI and our own Collin Wilson side with Ohio State.

Market ratings also side with the Buckeyes, as home-field advantage at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium is worth more than 1.5 points.

New Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith picked up the pace in the season opener, running a play every 24.5 seconds in the first half with the first-team offense on the field — a stark difference from last year's nation-slowest 31.1.

Despite an uptick in heavy personnel, Smith also got his star receivers involved early and often, targeting Jeremiah Smith nine times and UTSA transfer Devin McCuin seven times.

Last year's offensive concerns have been directly addressed right out of the gate.

But this game will be won and lost at the line of scrimmage. Both teams have had some concerns on the offensive line.

On more than one occasion, the Buckeyes' line was beaten in one-on-one opportunities by Ball State pass rushers in Week 1. Last year, Texas' line was a disaster, and NFL prospect Trevor Goosby began this season with injury concerns.

Against a better Buckeyes defensive front, we'll see if this unit has truly turned it around. Rarely harassed by Texas State's front, Arch Manning was nearly perfect, completing 20-of-27 passes for 291 yards and four touchdowns.

In a game with razor-thin margins and top-end NFL talent at every level, it's likely a game of who makes the first mistake. Both offenses looked flawless, and Ohio State even flashed an explosive run game in the second half.

In line with our experts, there's an ever-so-slight nod to Ohio State here.

Just like with the spread, our experts at Action Network are split across the board when it comes to this NFL-esque point total. Six of our 12 voters lean under 48.5 points, four lean over and two see this as a fair line.

In recent history, big regular-season games between giants result in low-scoring slugfests.

Look no further than last year's showdown between these two teams for a 14-7 final in Columbus. Miami and Notre Dame dueled to a 27-24 finish to open 2025, too.

Players and coaches — many of whom are new to the programs — typically head into these marquee games tightly wound and looking for a way to control something (the clock, the ground game, anything).

It's a boxing match of poking and prodding for any weakness. That results in a slow pace and conservative game planning.

Turns out, both teams had a major issue with conservative play-calling all season long. But out of the gate, both teams also made it clear that would not be the case moving forward.

Expect a significant increase in Ohio State's tempo on offense, and Texas' defense in its first game under Will Muschamp showed some vulnerabilities (which Texas State failed to capitalize on).

Beau Sparks, good as he is for the Bobcats, is not Jeremiah Smith, and the opportunity against Texas' defense comes against its secondary.

But the concern on that end is the Buckeyes' tackles holding up. Multiple times they were beat against Ball State and, of course, the Cardinals don't roster anyone with the pass-rushing prowess of future first-round NFL pick Colin Simmons.

Expect an aggressive approach from Muschamp up front while attempting to put a lid on the top of Smith and poach on McCuin.

For those reasons — and the fact that we haven't seen Texas' line tested since last year — our team leans slightly under to fair value on the total.

Devin McCuin Over 46.5 Receiving Yards (Play to 49.5)

Bringing in top-five high school recruiting classes on an annual basis, Ohio State doesn't dip into the transfer portal often, but it did to bring in UTSA transfer Devin McCuin.

In his Buckeyes debut, McCuin made an immediate impact with six catches for 97 yards and a touchdown. He quickly forged a connection with quarterback Julian Sayin and benefited from the attention that Jeremiah Smith draws.

While Smith will get his, teams will spend much of this season trying to take him away, and Texas is no exception. In two games against Texas, Smith has a total of seven receptions for 46 yards.

If you want to fade Smith against the Longhorns for a third time, feel free. However, I'll instead back McCuin, who has plenty of incentive to have a big night.

McCuin is a Jacksonville, Texas, native, and Texas didn't recruit him either out of high school or as a transfer. While he didn't grow up a Texas fan, most Texas high school football players at least want the opportunity to play for the state's flagship program and typically try to make the Longhorns pay when they don't get it.

Additionally, McCuin has an important role playing opposite Smith as the Buckeyes look for a third consecutive win over the Longhorns.

In last year's matchup, it was Carnell Tate, not Smith, who made the game's big play with a 40-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, which proved to be the deciding score.

Tate finished with two catches for 49 yards, which is just about what we need from McCuin this week.

Given that Sayin won't be making his first start this time around, the Buckeyes' passing game should have more volume this time around, which benefits McCuin as well as their other receivers.

The Boston Celtics have reportedly expressed interest in signing former lottery pick Devin Carter. The guard was recently waived by the Atlanta Hawks. The Celtics are the only team that has been reported to have interest.

Devin Carter is a guard who was a recent lottery pick in the 2024 NBA draft. He spent his first two seasons in the NBA with the Sacramento Kings before being traded to the Atlanta Hawks this offseason. He was eventually waived by Atlanta and placed on waivers.

The Celtics were immediately reported as interested by Jake Fischer , and news could be announced once Carter clears waivers.

Carter has not been given much of an opportunity in the NBA. He has been stuck behind other guards in Sacramento and has not been able to stick in the rotation. He has played in 74 games (12 starts) in his two seasons. Carter averaged a career-high 18.4 minutes a night last season.

Carter averaged 8.9 in 2025-26, but was severely inefficient. He shot 41% from the field and 26% from three. He would need to find some efficiency if he plans on becoming a piece of the Boston Celtics in 2026.

Carter is very skilled on the defensive end of the floor, and that is where a majority of his potential comes from. The Celtics could see some similarities between Carter's defensive skill set and Derrick White's, although that would represent the best-case scenario for the young guard. He still has a very long way to go.

The Celtics would be taking a bet in potential here if they go through with the signing. It's a low-risk, high-reward type of move that makes a lot of sense.

Carter would be able to learn from veteran Mike Conley, who could be another template as the type of player he could become.

articles.title: ‘I plan on playing’: Rome Odunze questionable but is optimistic he’ll suit up for Bears opener
articles.summary: CHICAGO — Chicago Bears receiver Rome Odunze was again a limited participant in practice Friday and has been listed as questionable for Sunday’s season opene...
articles.body:
CHICAGO — Chicago Bears receiver Rome Odunze was again a limited participant in practice Friday and has been listed as questionable for Sunday's season opener against the Carolina Panthers .

Odunze injured his right calf last week in practice. He sat out practice Monday and Tuesday before returning to the practice field Thursday and Friday in a limited fashion.

Coach Ben Johnson said the Bears would finalize a plan for Odunze later in the day Friday after practice.

"Our plan was to get him (to) practice yesterday and today, and we'll assess where he's at after that," Johnson said Friday morning. "He's looked good from my perspective, but we also got a long season coming up on us and we want to do what's right for him for the long term as well."

Odunze said he feels "great" and was optimistic that he will play Sunday.

"I'm feeling ready to go," Odunze said. "I doubt I'm questionable. I know there's a way everybody goes about things, but I feel pretty good. I was out there today (in practice). I plan on playing."

Additionally, the Bears listed backup quarterback Tyson Bagent (back), offensive tackle Ozzy Trapilo (knee) and safety Xavier Woods (groin) as questionable. Trapilo and Woods were limited participants in practice. Bagent did not participate in practice Friday.

If Bagent is sidelined, 38-year-old veteran quarterback Case Keenum would serve as the backup to Caleb Williams . Keenum has appeared in 80 career regular-season games, but he has not played in the regular season since 2023 as a member of the Houston Texans .

The Bears, of course, hope they won't need their backup quarterback with Williams set to start Year 3. Williams has been durable over his first two seasons, starting all 17 games in 2024 and 2025.

But the Bears still need to have their contingency plans, and Sunday against the Panthers it could be Keenum as the backup. The Bears don't have any other quarterbacks on the roster or practice squad.

Bagent dealt with a hamstring injury during training camp but was healthy for the final preseason game two weeks ago. His back injury appears to be something new. He participated in practice as recently as Tuesday.

At safety, Woods' groin injury could be relevant to the defensive game plan this week. Woods had been trending toward starting at safety in the final weeks of training camp. The Bears also have an experienced veteran in Cam Lewis available at the position.

Trapilo isn't likely to play this week and has yet to participate in team drills after recovering from a January knee injury.

As for Odunze, if he's unable to go Sunday, that could lead to more opportunities for the remaining receivers.

"We always have contingency plans going into it," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said this week. "That's our job. That's what we're supposed to do. So if something happens and they say he's full-go on Sunday, he can't go on Sunday, we're ready for that. That's our job to be prepared for that as best we can."

Luther Burden III is fully healthy after missing some time during training camp with a groin injury. Kalif Raymond , Jahdae Walker and Zavion Thomas are likely to see action. The Bears have three receivers on the practice squad whom they could call up for game day: Kaden Davis , Scotty Miller and J.P. Richardson.

Last year, Odunze missed the final five regular-season games with a foot injury. But before the calf injury last week, he had been fully healthy throughout training camp.

"Coming off last year, you hate to have injuries," Odunze said. "So through the offseason and through this training camp I've been healthy, and I think you can't take those things for granted. Being healthy is definitely a big priority, and it's been a priority for me over this training camp and going into this game. I'm super excited with where I'm at and I'm hopeful that it will continue all season long."

articles.title: Texas State vs UTSA predictions: Why 2 writers differ in I-35 football picks for 2026
articles.summary: Texas State and UTSA football beat writers get together to discuss which team is favored in Saturday's I-35 Rivalry game.
articles.body:
Since G.J. Kinne took control of the program prior to the 2023 season, Texas State football and UTSA have some striking similarities. Both programs are led by coaches with East Texas roots, as Roadrunners' seventh-year leader Jeff Traylor once coached Kinne at Gilmer High School.

UTSA and Texas State entered 2026 with identical 23-16 records over the previous three seasons and made financial push toward elite status in the Group of Six. The Bobcats won the past two in the series, including a 49-10 rout the last time the teams met in San Marcos, but the Roadrunners won the first five matchups. Naturally this week, bragging rights hang in the balance.

Both programs' hopes for 2026 rest on standout quarterbacks who turned down possible transfer opportunities at bigger programs, as Texas State's Brad Jackson and UTSA's Owen McCown stuck around for one more clash. Ahead of another matchup at 2:30 p.m. Saturday in scorching San Marcos, the stakes of the I-35 rivalry have never been higher.

Austin American-Statesman Texas State beat reporter Caleb Yum and San Antonio Express-News UTSA beat reporter Greg Luca make a case for each team's advantages and pick a winner.

Luca's case for UTSA: Now healthy after offseason surgery to heal a sports hernia and time to rest other injuries that nagged him last year, Owen McCown looked sharp in the Roadrunners' opener. With his mobility and athleticism unlocked again, UTSA will likely sprinkle in a little quarterback run game to keep Texas State off balance.

The Roadrunners seemed to adapt quickly to new offensive coordinator Rick Bowie, who implemented a couple of fresh Air Raid concepts and ushered in a shift away from the tight end-heavy sets that were previously hallmarks of Traylor's offense. Running back Will Henderson is an explosive threat because of his elite speed as a former state champion sprinter, and receiver David Amador gives the Roadrunners a versatile gadget option. Expect UTSA to have plenty of tricks up its sleeve, as well as a bevy of new plays that were kept safely out of sight in Week 1.

Yum's case for Texas State: Henderson is priority one for the Bobcats. In a perfect world, Texas State stops the run without committing extra men to the box, keeping enough bodies in the secondary to limit explosives through the air. It might sound like wishful thinking, but the Bobcats limited UT's running backs to 4.3 yards per rush last week on 30 carries - 3.4 without Hollywood Smothers' early 45-yard burst.

Even if the defense is forced to commit to stopping the ground game, McCown hasn't lit it up against Texas State in the past: he's averaged 162 passing yards on 50% completion in two losses. The Bobcats' secondary didn't perform well in Week 1, but they did face an elite receiving tandem. Defensive backs Ryan Nolan and cornerback Trez Moore are proven contributors, and this might be the most talented group of defensive backs Texas State has ever fielded. The pass rush should be better after playing a Texas tackle duo that could be playing in the NFL next season.

Yum's case for Texas State: Traylor has heaped praise on Bobcats quarterback Brad Jackson leading up to the game, for good reason. He accounted for three touchdowns in the last matchup and looked confident in Week 1 against a talented Texas defense. The San Antonio product gets homefield advantage and wide receivers Chris Dawn Jr. and Beau Sparks are deadly in one-on-one matchups, posing serious questions for the Roadrunners' secondary. Texas State's offensive line hasn't missed a beat, and running backs Jaylen Jenkins and Davian Jackson could be a menace, especially playing off the quarterback run game.

Texas State cannot afford to turn the ball over. The Bobcats need to convert in the red zone and avoid a close game - kicker Dylan Cunanan missed two relatively short field-goal attempts in Week 1.

Luca's case for UTSA: The case for UTSA's defense is thin, likely falling on the shoulders of the cornerbacks. The group is perhaps the deepest and most talented on the defense. JUCO transfer Asaad Chapman started in his UTSA debut last week, joining his talented twin brother Ahamad in the rotation. Oklahoma State transfer RJ Lester grabbed a starting spot he was supposed to claim last season if not for the discovery of a heart condition that sidelined him through his first year in the program. Zach Morris is finally healthy after being limited for most of his tenure at UTSA, and Jakevian Rodgers has continued to develop during his fourth year.

Starting safeties Elijah Newell and Cam Upshaw are unproven; the pass rush appears minimal beyond Cam Cooper, and the defensive line struggled with containment even against UTRGV. Sounds like a formula for disaster against Texas State, unless the corners can lock up. The next best bet is trying to hold in the red zone and praying for more missed field goals from the Bobcats.

Luca's case for UTSA: The Roadrunners' fan base can't afford to endure another slow start. In totality, UTSA's 7-6 campaigns the past two years have been fine, maintaining Traylor's streak of reaching a bowl in every year of his tenure. But the Roadrunners had to rally after opening 3-5 in 2024 and 3-4 last season, achieving some of their best moments with minimal buzz and fewer eyes on the program.

A win Saturday could fix three problems: the slow starts, the 3-10 road record the past two years, and the disappointment of two straight losses to the Bobcats. A setback with a sure loss at Texas looming next week would send the Roadrunners careening back toward the doldrums. For UTSA, this is the most important matchup in the history of the I-35 rivalry.

Yum's case for Texas State: Starting a season 0-2 is bad. That's obvious. More importantly, Texas State needs to prove it can handle strong midmajor competition if it wants to strengthen its - and the Pac-12's - case for a College Football Playoff berth.

After the Bobcats stagnated in 2025, Kinne revamped the defense, hoping to get past the seven- to eight-win benchmark that's become less impressive over the years. Jackson returned, along with his two 1,000-yard receivers. Texas State has no more excuses. Lose to UTSA - which looks to be the less-talented team on paper - at home, and it's fair to question whether the Bobcats' formula has run dry. North Texas is not an easy Week 3 opponent. Texas State could enter Pac-12 play 1-3, which would be a huge disappointment for a program that entered the season looking for a conference championship.

articles.title: NFL Week 1 Bears-Panthers Predictions: Which run defense will step up?
articles.summary: This feels like a lot of ground-and-pound upcoming for the Bears and Panthers. @BryanOrenchuk explores it here.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers have not won a Week 1 game since 2021, but they are coming off a playoff season in 2025. Could they beat the Chicago Bears outright at home or at least cover the spread?

Much has been made of the trade that brought Caleb Williams to Chicago and Bryce Young to Carolina. Since the two QBs have taken over for their respective squads, the Bears have gone 16-18 (11-6 under Ben Johnson), and the Panthers have gone 15-36.

Both teams are coming off strong seasons with playoff appearances led by their run games, and both teams made substantial acquisitions this offseason, especially on defense. Chicago signed S Coby Bryant and LB Devin Bush while Carolina added LB Devin Lloyd and Edge Jaelan Phillips . Obviously, Chicago fans know Bryant will miss most of the year with an injury, but the question remains for both teams.

Can they slow down their opponent's offense this week?

For a Chicago defense that allowed the 6th most rushing yards a season ago, the Panthers know they have to establish the run and build off their 2025 season, when they ranked in the top 20 in both rushing yards and attempts per game. Chicago will be leaning heavily on a couple rookies, Jordan van den Berg and Jayden Loving, and 9th-year pro Kentavius Street , whom Bears DC Dennis Allen said had the strongest camp of any DT on the roster .

For the Panthers, the addition of Lloyd and Phillips will most certainly help, but the Panthers defense still relies on the play of All-World DT Derrick Brown to slow down opposing offenses. Especially the run game. That said, the edge for best DL seems to go to Carolina in this one. However, in his first 3 career Week 1 starts, Bryce Young has thrown a combined 2 TDs and 6 INTs and has yet to throw for more than 200 yards. Which leads even more credence to the idea that the Panthers should " Keep Pounding " the ball on the ground this week.

Our friends at FanDuel Sportsbook currently have the Bears as 3-point favorites for this week's contest in Carolina. If you think the Bears will win outright, the moneyline is at -176, with the point total over/under at 47.5.

I am predicting a 31-20 Bears win, with both D'Andre Swift and Chuba Hubbard to lead their teams with over 70 yards rushing each – and that'll hit the over on their betting lines in this one, with Swift currently at 63.5 and Hubbard at 50.5.

articles.title: Washington Secondary Looks to Replicate Impressive Opening Performance
articles.summary: While the Huskies' front seven showed out in Week One, the secondary was sure to showcase its playmaking abilities.
articles.body:
Ryan Walters' defense certainly lived up to the hype with its Week One performance. The Washington Huskies ' second-year defensive coordinator orchestrated a strong game plan against Washington State quarterback Caden Pinnick and the Cougars, allowing just 10 points and less than 250 yards of total offense. While the front seven has received praise for its efforts, and rightfully so, the secondary also put together an impressive showing.

Pinnick, who was named the Big Sky Freshman of the Year in 2025 at UC Davis, faced the Huskies last season, posting just 50 yards passing with a touchdown and an interception. This time around, things weren't too different for the young quarterback. The Huskies picked off Pinnick twice, the first coming at the hands of freshman Jeron Jones and the latter being the game-sealing interception by fourth-year safety Alex McLaughlin.

While creating extra possessions for the offense, the impact went far beyond forcing turnovers. Three out of Washington's four leading tacklers in the game were McLaughlin and cornerbacks Dylan Robinson and Emmanuel Karnley. While Robinson was hardly targeted in the game, Karnley came up with two pass deflections in his Husky debut after transferring in from Virginia.

"I think what you get from those guys is a willingness and a want to," head coach Jedd Fisch said of the secondary's physicality. "Sometimes with the DB's, it's a willingness, but is there a want to, right? When you have guys that are willing and wanting to, that's, I think, the difference between having a good defense and having a great defense."

Similar to much of Washington's roster, the secondary has a balanced blend of experienced playmakers and young talent. The youth is headlined by freshman standout Jeron Jones, along with Robinson and his classmate, second-year safety Rylon-Dillard Allen, while McLaughlin and nickelback Rahshawn Clark highlight the physicality and playmaking abilities that Fisch has lauded.

As Fisch and Walters aim to piece together another stout defensive performance, their ball-hawking secondary will have another big opportunity against a Utah State team that threw four interceptions in a losing effort to Idaho State to open the season. The Huskies kick things off against the Aggies at 12:30 on the Big Ten Network.

articles.title: WRC Chile: Oliver Solberg urges “clever” approach as tyre fears grow for Saturday
articles.summary: The Rally Chile leader holds a 10.1s advantage over Elfyn Evans, but drivers expect Saturday’s longer, warmer stages to put Hankook’s tyres under much greate...
articles.body:
Rally Chile leader Oliver Solberg has stressed the need to drive "clever" as World Rally Championship crews expect tyre-punishing stages on Saturday.

The Toyota driver enjoyed an issue free day on Friday to move into a 10.1s lead over team-mate Elfyn Evans, after handling the tricky muddy conditions caused by overnight rain.

However, Saturday is set to serve up a completely different challenge with crews poised to tackle 139.2km of stages that are expected to run in much warmer and dry temperatures that will put the tyres under stress. To avoid a repeat of the punctures and delaminations suffered last time out in Paraguay, Rally1 crews have an increased allocation of Hankook tyres for the weekend.

"Tomorrow is a completely different type of rally and it is important to be clever. I tried to learn a little bit about that today with the car. Today was important to learn for tomorrow. It will be the most important day," said Solberg.

"For tomorrow the gap is not a lot, and it is good to have the gap and when it is going to be hard for the tyres, we don't have to take the final risk. But anything can happen to anyone, especially if it is going to be hot and dry, and with the tyres we have, you never know."

Adrien Fourmaux, Alexandre Coria, Hyundai Shell Mobis World Rally Team Hyundai i20 N Rally1

Friday's stages ran without any tyre issues, with Takamoto Katsuta's retirement on the opening stage the only major incident among the Rally1 crews.

However, nine-time world champion Sébastien Ogier expects "many things" to happen on Saturday and is hoping that he can avoid drama. Last year's Chile winner will begin Saturday 19.7s from the lead, sitting in fourth, 1.7s behind Hyundai's third-placed Adrien Fourmaux.

"There is a long way to go and we expect many things to happen tomorrow [Saturday] and the tyres are going to be suffering much more tomorrow. We might see more issues on that topic and let's hope we can stay out of trouble," said Ogier.

Sébastien Ogier, Vincent Landais, Toyota Gazoo Racing WRT Toyota GR Yaris Rally1

Fourmaux shared Ogier's view adding: "Nothing really happened today but tomorrow I think more things will happen."

M-Sport-Ford's Josh McErlean believes the chances of a clean day for the WRC field on Saturday will be low.

"It is a completely different character of roads. The stages are very long and demanding and tyre wear will be crucial. If everyone gets through tomorrow cleanly I will be surprised," said McErlean.

Esapekka Lappi, Enni Malkonen, Hyundai World Rally Team Hyundai i20 N Rally1

Saturday's stages are expected to rub salt into the wounds for Hyundai's Esapekka Lappi, who feels his rally is already over after struggling for confidence and speed in Friday's wet and dry stages.

Recalled to the third Hyundai seat for the first time since Rally Finland last month, Lappi cut a frustrated figure after being unable to push behind the wheel of his i20 N Rally1. The Finn ended the day in ninth and will now face the effects of cleaning starting second on the road on Saturday.

"We tried to change something [on the set up] for the afternoon but we went in the wrong direction. The starting position for Saturday is really bad so the weekend is basically over. But that is life," said Lappi.

"The road position is so bad. There is so much cleaning tomorrow there is no chance to do anything special. I think the mind is fine it is just in some corners you try to go a bit faster and then there is a reminder you shouldn't as you go wide with the rear. I'm trying.

"I know how to drive and in the morning in my Rally2 car I would have been faster because that car does what I want, but this car doesn't do what I want."

articles.title: Report: Boston Celtics interested in signing former Providence star Devin Carter
articles.summary: Carter, a 24-year-old guard who played at nearby Providence College, was picked up with the 13th pick of the 2024 Draft by Sacramento.
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics are reportedly interested in signing former Providence College standout Devin Carter , according to the Stein Line contributor Jake Fischer. "The Boston Celtics have shown interest in signing Devin Carter," posted Fischer on social media Friday (Sep. 11) afternoon, noting that the West Palm Beach, Florida native will first need to clear waivers after having been dealt to the Atlanta Hawks earlier this offseason, then cut.

Carter, a 24-year-old point guard who played his college ball at nearby Providence College of Rhode Island, was picked up with the 13th overall pick of the 2024 NBA Draft by the Sacramento Kings , and put up 8.9 points, 3.3 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and just under a steal in 18.4 minutes per game.

The former Friar shot just 26.3 percent from beyond the arc, 71.3 percent from the free throw line, and 41.4 percent from the floor overall in that campaign, likely contributing to the decision of the Hawks to part ways with Carter.

But the former lottery pick is a dogged defender who fits the sort of profile valued by Boston in the past, so a low-cost gamble on a second-draft player makes sense for Boston.

That is, should another team not swoop in to secure his services in the meantime.

articles.title: Cowboys player carted off practice field expected to miss ‘significant time’ according to Stephen Jones
articles.summary: The Cowboys are going to need to adjust their plans ahead of Sunday Night Football.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have suffered a potentially significant injury just days before their NFL season opener against the New York Giants .

Running back Malik Davis was carted off the practice field Friday, and Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones indicated the injury could keep him sidelined for an extended period.

Aug 1, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys running back Malik Davis (20) carries the ball at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Davis was forced to leave Friday's practice after suffering a hip injury, and the Cowboys quickly ruled him out for Sunday night's opener. The initial concern surrounding the injury was confirmed when Jones described it as "pretty serious" and said it could keep Davis out for "some period of time." The team was still awaiting final details on the injury.

That is a brutal development for Davis, who had seemingly earned a major opportunity in Dallas.

After battling Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah throughout training camp and the preseason, Davis emerged as the Cowboys' No. 2 running back behind Javonte Williams . He was expected to receive meaningful touches in a backfield that was already relatively thin.

Now, Dallas could be forced to completely change its plans.

Cowboys suddenly have a major problem at running back

Jun 16, 2026; Dallas, TX, USA; Dallas Cowboys running back Malik Davis (20) goes through a drill during practice at the Ford Center at the Star Training Facility in Frisco, Texas. Mandatory Credit: Chris Jones-Imagn Images

With Davis unavailable, Emari Demercado is expected to take on a significantly larger role behind Williams. Demercado was claimed off waivers by Dallas on Aug. 31 and was already the only other traditional running back on the 53-man roster.

The Cowboys do have Israel Abanikanda on the practice squad, meaning he could potentially be elevated for Sunday's game against the Giants. Dallas could also explore adding another veteran running back if Davis is ultimately facing a lengthy absence.

For Williams, the injury could mean far more work immediately. Dallas did not necessarily enter the season planning to make him a true workhorse back, but Davis' injury could force that issue right away.

Losing a player who had just won the RB2 job days before Week 1 is a major blow for Dallas, and if Davis truly misses significant time, the Cowboys will have to find another solution quickly.

articles.title: Ryan Garcia Vs. Conor Benn Is Tomorrow — Here's The Expected Ring-Walk Time
articles.summary: Ryan Garcia weighed 145.5 and Conor Benn 146 for Saturday at T-Mobile Arena. Full weigh-in results, start times and the expected ring-walk time.
articles.body:
We heard a lot about Conor Benn struggling to make weight for Saturday's clash with Ryan Garcia, but that didn't appear to be the case on Friday. Benn weighed in at a ready 146 pounds on Friday morning and Garcia was even lighter at 145.5 pounds. Both men appear to be ready and in great physical condition, which could help to produce a memorable championship fight. I must admit, this one is even more special because it is actually for a world title. Need info on when the men will walk? Let's talk Garcia-Benn.

Da'Mazion Vanhouter vs. Raphael Akpejiori

There is no rehydration clause in this contract, which matters more than the scale did. Benn has said he expects to enter the ring around 175 pounds. Garcia projects himself around 157. Nothing in the deal stops either number. Garcia also spent fight week insisting Benn was nowhere near the limit, then stepped on the scale half a pound lighter than the man he was accusing.

Garcia and Benn weren't the only ones to make weight on the card. Like Saturday's Noche UFC card, every fighter on the prelims and main event was on weight. You can see all the official weights below.

Who wins Garcia-Benn? It comes down to a few things. Can Benn handle Garcia's hand speed? If he cannot, it could be a short night for him. If Benn can handle the hand speed and he can get inside to make it a dirtier, grimy battle, he could find some success — especially in the later rounds. Garcia is one of the most talented fighters in the world, but when he doesn't land his left hook and abandons his jab, he is beatable by the top competition. We'll see if Benn can prove himself to be in that number on Saturday night.

"So…Just continue to get better at that, continue to watch guys like Adrian Peterson , and just a lot of like, old film, to dissect where their free hitter was before their play even started, has been pretty unique as a process."

Robinson has studied the film at the urging of the team's running backs coach, Michael Pitre. It has given him a sixth sense on knowing which tackle he needs to break upon entering the second level of the opposing team's defense.

The Adrian Peterson film room experience has emboldened and excited Robinson ahead of a crucial season for Stefanski's team.

"It was pretty special," Robinson said. "It's just those guys that elevate it to a different level, and watching that film and watching those guys, that's how you know that you're special and he won the MVP that year, and I think that was a big reason why."

Robinson has the talent to bring home his first MVP award this season, and now he has a better concept of how to make it happen. It starts Sunday against the Steelers in a game that will provide clues as to whether he is up to the challenge.

articles.title: Good Sports: A new era for Fresno City College football
articles.summary: Head coach Josh Brown takes over for longtime FCC head coach Tony Caviglia after the Rams Hall of Famer retired last season.
articles.body:
The Rams are off and running into the 2026 season.

For the first time in 27 years, a new coach leads them out onto the field.

Head coach Josh Brown takes over for longtime FCC head coach Tony Caviglia after the Rams Hall of Famer retired last season.

"When it first opened up, the first guy I called was Coach C and said, 'You think I should go for it?' and he said, 'Yeah, absolutely.'"

Brown is stepping in to fill the void of a legend at Fresno City College.

It's his first head coaching gig in over 20 years of coaching experience after stops at UTEP, Cal Poly and Morehead State.

"I've recruited this school for over 20 years as a Division I coach, so I always knew this is a good spot," he said.

He's bringing that experience to the JUCO level, where Brown's focus has always been clear.

"I was a junior college product myself," he said. "I truly believe that I can change these guys' lives though, and that's the main focus of our culture."

The Rams opened up the season two weeks ago against Sierra on the road, and while the start was less than ideal, a tush push for the win with eight seconds left sure made for a fun bus ride home.

"We were down 8-0 with 14:30 left in the first quarter, so I had some thoughts where I was like, maybe this head coaching isn't for me," he said.

A tush push for the win with eight seconds left sure made for a fun bus ride home.

"Everyone was all happy," says quarterback Christian English. "We were hyped on the bus. It just shows we have no quit, and we're willing to do whatever it takes to win the deal."

The Rams doubled that win total with a 24-10 win in the home opener on Saturday, as Brown and the Rams push for a title in his first season.

"We want to win, and I think he, obviously, wants to win, too," English said. "I think our main goal is just to be champions and be the best we could be."

articles.title: Hewett and Reid secure sixth US Open doubles title
articles.summary: British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid come from a set and a break down to win the men's wheelchair doubles title for the sixth time at the US Open.
articles.body:
British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid came from a set and a break down to win the men's wheelchair doubles title for the sixth time as a partnership at the US Open.

Five years on from their most recent title at Flushing Meadows, the legendary pair battled back to beat Spain's Martin de la Puente and Ruben Spaargaren of the Netherlands 2-6 6-3 10-7 in a match tie-break.

It is a remarkable 30th Grand Slam doubles title for 34-year-old Reid, 11 years on from the Scot's first, with 26 of them coming alongside Hewett.

"We've not won here for five years so this is something we've been desperate for and highly motivated for," Hewett, 28, said.

"It won't be the last, we've got plenty more doubles to play in the future.

"These are the sort of matches we want to play in front of such an amazing crowd. I'm glad we could put on a bit of a show for you tonight."

Reid added: "It's been more than 13 years we've been playing together and he's not sick of me yet. Hopefully we've got a few more years left in us."

The title looked a long way off as top seeds Hewett and Reid struggled in the first set, losing six games in a row after going up 2-0 early.

De le Puente and Spaargaren kept the pressure up in the second and looked in control after breaking to lead 3-2.

However, Hewett and Reid hit back immediately and the momentum of the match switched in an instant.

The British duo took four consecutive games to win the set and force the 10-point match tie-break.

It went back and forth in the early stages but Hewett and Reid opened up a gap to lead 7-4 and despite a double fault from Hewett at 8-6, they kept their composure to seal their third major win of 2026.

Earlier, Hewett booked his place in the men's wheelchair singles final. The second seed was leading 6-0 3-0 when Argentina's Gustavo Fernandez retired injured.

He will face defending champion and top seed Tokito Oda of Japan, who has won the previous three majors in 2026 and is going for the calendar Grand Slam.

Meanwhile, Briton Matthew Knoesen had a day to remember as he won both the junior boys wheelchair singles and doubles titles.

The singles crown was claimed with a 6-0 6-2 win over Australia's Sonny Rennison, while Knoesen partnered with Hirofumi Inoue of Japan to win the doubles title - they beat fellow Briton Will Barton and Italy's Lorenzo Politano 6-1 6-0.

articles.title: Diamondbacks' Dominican prospect is a scam victim, per detailed report
articles.summary: A ProPublica article exposed a baseball scammer who preys on poor families in the Dominican Republic, including one in the Diamondbacks organization.
articles.body:
A Dominican Summer League player in the Arizona Diamondbacks organization, Belfi Rivera, is at the heart of a deflating story that dropped on ProPublica about young baseball players in the Dominican Republic being preyed on and scammed.

Gus Garcia-Roberts, an investigative reporter who specializes in sports, released the article on Thursday, Sept. 10. Rivera is at the forefront as Garcia-Roberts exposes Santo Caraballo, whom Garcia-Roberts describes as "one of the most notorious moneylenders profiting from Dominican baseball," for receiving $950,000 of Rivera's money despite not having anything to do with Rivera's development.

That $950,000 is part of a $1.8 million deal the Diamondbacks pledged to pay him after he turned 16. Garcia-Roberts also found that these deals are made verbally, so no records can be found if a team decides they do not want to pay the kids.

MLB finds more players in the Dominican Republic than anywhere outside of the United States, so the league sees the country as a hotbed for talent. They work to sell the kids and families on a dream that they can become the next Ketel Marte , Geraldo Perdomo or whichever Dominican star they look up to. Oftentimes, like in Rivera's case, the players and families they talk to come from poor financial backgrounds.

Arizona Diamondbacks' 3-game series at Kansas City Royals in photos

Rivera was 14 years old when he was told the family's struggles would soon be over. However, in two and a half years, the $1.8 million was almost completely gone.

John Carmona, Belfi's trainer, got his 35% commission. That was $630,000. This, plus the $950,000 that Caraballo got his hands on, left Rivera with little.

Caraballo took advantage of Rivera and his parents by offering loans with excessive interest rates. Caraballo convinced Rivera and his family that he was trustworthy because Hall of Famer David Ortiz was his business partner.

Ortiz told Garcia-Roberts that he cut Caraballo off at least a year and a half ago. However, Ortiz also posted a video of him and Caraballo together on a private jet to Puerto Rico in September 2025, drinking and dancing as they headed to a Bad Bunny concert.

The promise of becoming Ortiz, the promise that Ortiz was behind the plan, targeting a poor family and finding ways to exploit Rivera's parents' struggle with literacy has placed Rivera in a tough situation.

articles.title: Charlotte Bobcats jersey history No. 1 Ryan Hollins 2006-2009
articles.summary: Former UCLA product Ryan Hollins spent two and a half seasons with Charlotte, playing in 105 games for the Bobcats.
articles.body:
Backup center Ryan Hollins was the fourth player in Charlotte Hornets franchise history to wear the No. 1, doing so for a brief stretch as a member of the Charlotte Bobcats. A former No. 50 overall pick out of UCLA, Hollins played two and a half seasons in Charlotte before being traded along with Matt Carroll to the Dallas Mavericks for DeSagana Diop.

In 105 games for the Bobcats, Hollins averaged 2.6 points, 1.7 rebounds, 0.2 assists, 0.2 steals and 0.5 blocks. Following his time in Charlotte, Hollins would go on to play seven more seasons, giving himself an impressive 10-year NBA career. In 518 career appearances, Hollins averaged 3.7 points, 2.2 rebounds, 0.3 assists, 0.2 steals and 0.5 blocks. Since his playing days, Hollins has served as a basketball analyst and pundit for a variety of different outlets.
